rfp_requirements.title: Include staffing for maximum throughput
rfp_requirements.description: The Plan shall include the number of adequately trained personnel anticipated for periods of maximum throughput.

rfp_requirements.title: Monitor and manage Wait Times throughout Contract term
Limit Average Customer Wait Time to 30 Minutes
rfp_requirements.description: Ensure the average Customer Wait Time at a CIF does not exceed 30 minutes in any two contiguous operating hours.

rfp_requirements.title: Limit Average Customer Wait Time to 40 Minutes After O-30 Violation
rfp_requirements.description: Ensure the average Customer Wait Time at a CIF does not exceed 40 minutes, and for each 10-minute increasing interval following a violation recorded per SLA O-30.

rfp_requirements.title: Limit Monthly Average Customer Wait Time to 25 Minutes After O-32 Violation
rfp_requirements.description: Ensure the CIFs do not have a monthly average customer wait time in excess of 25 minutes, and for each additional 10-minute increasing interval following a violation recorded per SLA O-32.

rfp_requirements.title: Implement, operate, and maintain Wait Time system
Use Wait Time data to generate SCM requested reports
Maintain acceptable SLA performance levels
Repair or replace defective/worn-out equipment
Monitor system availability, network, database, transactions, errors, outages
Obtain prior SCM approval for downtime in writing
Promote Critical Severity fixes to production after UAT
rfp_requirements.description: Once a Critical Severity Defect change passes UAT, it must be promoted to production within one Business Day of SCM approval.

rfp_requirements.title: Promote Critical Severity Defect fixes to production within one Business Day of State approval
rfp_requirements.description: Once a Critical Severity Defect change passes UAT, it shall be promoted to production within one (1) Business Day of State approval.

rfp_requirements.title: Promote Moderate Severity Defect fixes to production within three Business Days of State approval
rfp_requirements.description: Once a Moderate Severity Defect change passes UAT, it shall be promoted to production within three (3) Business Days of State approval.

rfp_requirements.title: Promote Low Severity Defect fixes with next service release or within 90 Business Days
rfp_requirements.description: Once the Low Severity Defect change passes UAT it shall be promoted to production with the next service release or within 90 Business Days, whichever comes sooner.

rfp_requirements.title: Comply with SLAs during all Contract phases
rfp_requirements.description: Contractor must maintain and comply with all applicable service levels during Implementation, Operational, and Post-Operational phases shown in Section 5.8.

rfp_requirements.title: Ensure Motorist Hotline availability and tracking
rfp_requirements.description: Contractor must ensure Motorist Hotline is available to NJ State Motorists at all times and can handle, track, and report on all inquiries and complaints with on-demand reporting via the Management Console.

rfp_requirements.title: Utilize all existing CIFs
rfp_requirements.description: Contractor must utilize all CIFs presently available and may operate as many lanes/configurations as necessary to meet convenience and Wait Time standards.

rfp_requirements.title: Pay Liquidated Damages for Missed Contract Completion Dates
rfp_requirements.description: If Contractor cannot meet the Contract completion date for any task or subtask required to be completed by a date certain, Contractor agrees to be liable to pay liquidated damages to the State.

rfp_requirements.title: Notify SCM in Writing of Correction of Liquidated Damages Conditions
rfp_requirements.description: To seek termination of continued liquidated damages, the Contractor must correct the conditions for which damages were imposed and notify the State Contract Manager in writing that the condition(s) have been corrected.

rfp_requirements.title: Pay Balance of Liquidated Damages Within 30 Calendar Days
rfp_requirements.description: If funds owed by the State are insufficient to satisfy the liquidated damages assessed, pay the balance to the State of New Jersey within 30 Calendar Days of written notification of the assessment.

rfp_requirements.title: Liability for Unpaid Wages and Liquidated Damages
rfp_requirements.description: In the event of violation of the overtime clause, the Contractor and any responsible subcontractor shall be liable for unpaid wages and for liquidated damages of $27 per calendar day per affected individual worked in excess of forty hours without required overtime.

rfp_requirements.title: Withholding of Funds for Unpaid Wages and Liquidated Damages
rfp_requirements.description: Funds may be withheld from any moneys payable on account of work performed by the Contractor or subcontractor under this or any other Federal/federally-assisted contract with the same prime Contractor, as may be necessary to satisfy liabilities for unpaid wages and liquidated damages upon action of

rfp_requirements.title: Allow Service Level Audit
rfp_requirements.description: Contractor must allow the State (or a third party at State's discretion and expense) to audit conformance to the contract terms.

rfp_requirements.title: Establish standards for 30-minute average wait times and minimum operating cost
rfp_requirements.description: The chief administrator must establish standards designed to achieve average wait times of 30 minutes or less and to keep overall operating cost of facilities to a minimum.

rfp_requirements.title: Develop incentives system targeting 15-minute average wait times
rfp_requirements.description: The chief administrator must develop a system of incentives designed to achieve average wait times of 15 minutes or less.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
WORKING WITH PENNDOT TO MOVE THE I/M
PROGRAM FORWARD THROUGH ADAPTABILITY
AND INNOVATION
Parsons is uniquely positioned to deliver each requirement PennDOT has outlined for the new contract, enhancing what
works and innovating for the future. We’re fully committed to:
Applying innovation and advanced technology tailored to Pennsylvania’s Program
Ensuring station compliance
Employing advanced Cybersecurity protocols to protect against security threats
Eliminating PennDOT’s transition risk
Parsons appreciates PennDOT’s business. Throughout our response, we demonstrate our depth of experience, our
reliability, our compliance, and our adaptability. We have unmatched knowledge of PennDOT’s emissions and safety
programs, and we know what you require from your vendor. Most importantly, we won’t rest on our laurels; in this new
contract, we will demonstrate to PennDOT that we are the best vendor to bring the Program into the future.
Highlights of Parsons’ Technical Proposal
Secure Data and Information Management Systems. Our systems are reliable, and we are proud of the 99.99% uptime
of our Pennsylvania VIID. Program downtime is simply unacceptable to us, and our experien

AWS Partner Solutions Provider, AWS DevOps Competency Partner, and AWS Advanced Tier Services
Partner, and holds other designations. Our engineers and in-house security experts have more than 100 AWS
certifications, and Parsons has secured AWS’s commitment to support our Pennsylvania solution during our
implementation and ongoing utilization of AWS/AWS products. Our experience moving the Ontario DriveON program to
AWS allows us to implement our proposed update to the PA I/M Program VIID securely, without interruption in service
or uptime. We will upgrade our call center solution with new technology using ZenDesk and AmazonConnect as the
backbone of the system.
Station Compliance. Our operational goals align with PennDOT’s focus on station and inspector compliance. We
recognize the Program’s integrity and customer confidence are rooted in ensuring compliance. We will continually
adapt to improve our audit and hearing processes through innovation and enhanced auditor training. Parsons has in-
house professional oversight personnel with experience in the Pennsylvania Program. In this challenging labor market,
our teams are fully staffed, trained, and dependable.
Executive Summary ES-1

Equipment Certification. Parsons has certified all equipment used by the stations, from the days of tailpipe and
dynamometer testing to today’s OBD equipment. Our experienced and knowledgeable equipment certification team is
ready to support tomorrow’s vehicle communication protocols. We are not an equipment provider in Pennsylvania, and
this separation allows us to conduct impartial equipment testing, which is key to Program success and integrity. We
reliably ensure equipment performance that promotes consumer confidence.
Vendor Compliance. PennDOT expects its vendors to comply with all contract requirements. As part of Parsons’
compliance commitment, we will introduce our Service Level Tracking Application (SLTA) in AWS. The SLTA provides a
summary of the service level agreements that PennDOT has clearly stated in this RFP and identifies the delivery of the
task required, providing PennDOT with a way to ensure we meet our contractual obligations.
